metadata.title: Iron Triangle / Regulatory Capture
metadata.description: The classic political-science feedback loop. An interest group's political support helps a congressional subcommittee, which favorably treats an executive agency, which produces regulatory decisions that benefit the industry, which opens revolving-door career opportunities for former officials — and the cycle of mutual benefit locks in over time. All four edges are positive, so zero negative edges → reinforcing.
metadata.author: US Government Intelligent Textbook

nodes.label: Interest Group Political Support
nodes.description: Campaign donations, endorsements, expertise briefings, and constituent-mobilization help flowing from the industry's lobbyists to members of the relevant congressional subcommittee.

nodes.label: Committee Favorable Treatment of Agency
nodes.description: Favorable legislation, protected (or expanded) budget appropriations, and supportive oversight from the subcommittee to the executive agency that regulates the industry.

nodes.label: Agency Favorable Regulatory Decisions
nodes.description: Lenient enforcement, narrow rule interpretations, and slow-walked investigations from the agency toward the industry it regulates.

nodes.label: Revolving Door Career Flow
nodes.description: Job opportunities from the industry to former agency officials and committee staff. The anticipation of future hire creates a present-day incentive for lenient regulation.

edges.description: Industry money and political support translate into favorable committee action.
The committee uses its budget and oversight power to steer agency decisions toward industry-preferred outcomes.
Industry rewards lenient regulators with lucrative post-government jobs — and the credible promise of such jobs shapes current agency behavior.
Former regulators bring insider expertise and contacts to the industry, strengthening its political position for the next cycle.

loops.label: R: Iron Triangle
loops.description: Mutual benefit locks in over time. The fourth node (Revolving Door) is what makes the triangle 'iron' — it gives every actor a long-term reason to keep the cycle going.
loops.behavior_pattern: Self-reinforcing stability. Hard to break by changing any single actor — all four sides must change at once.
